transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I guess I came in because my behavior has been kind of intense lately. I went from barely settling into my new apartment to, just... suddenly saying yes to all these mentoring sessions. 

And I started taking on extra client prototypes for work, plus I decided to redesign my whole portfolio. It was like I suddenly had to fix my entire life in one single sprint. It's just been a lot, and I felt like I needed to come talk to someone about it.
During this intense period, have you needed much less sleep than usual and still felt rested?

Yeah, actually. Um, for several nights I was only getting maybe three or four hours of sleep. But I'd wake up convinced I was totally fine. I didn't feel tired at all, so I just thought... well, I should use the extra time to get ahead on my work.
During that time, did you feel unusually euphoric or unusually irritable?

Yeah, it was kind of a mix of both. Earlier this month, I felt almost... electric, I guess? Just really upbeat and on top of everything. But then, almost in the next minute, I would get incredibly irritable. 

I actually snapped at a contractor I work with, and my sister too, over just tiny delays. In the moment, it honestly felt like they were personally trying to block me from getting things done.
During these high-energy periods, have you had any beliefs that other people said were unrealistic or hard to believe?

No, I don't think so. I mean, nobody's ever told me I was being unrealistic or... believing things that weren't true. I just had a lot of ideas for my work and wanted to get them all done, but it was all normal stuff, just... a lot of it at once.
During this high-energy period, were you hospitalized because of your mood or behavior?
No, I haven't been hospitalized. It hasn't ever gotten to that point. I just... I get really busy and kind of intense about my projects, but I've never had to go to the hospital for it.
During that high-energy period, did your behavior cause serious problems at work, socially, or financially?

Well, it definitely caused some issues. I actually missed a pretty important design review at work because I was just... too caught up in everything else. And socially, I guess I've been pulling back. I've been avoiding my friends and even my family lately. I just feel embarrassed, honestly, about how scattered and... unreliable I've seemed to them.
Have you ever had a period lasting at least two weeks when you felt depressed or lost interest in most things nearly every day?

Yes. Actually, that's kind of where I'm at right now. Lately, I wake up with this heavy, gray feeling in my chest. It's just there every morning. And even when my apartment is completely quiet and nothing bad is happening at all, I feel like I could just start crying over something as small as a coffee mug left in the sink. It's been going on for a few weeks now.
During that high-energy period, did your behavior make you unable to function normally in your daily life?

Well, like I mentioned just a minute ago, I did miss that big design review at work. So, yeah, it definitely messed with my job. And I've been pulling away from my friends and family because I just feel so embarrassed about how scattered and unreliable I was being. So it definitely impacted my normal routine and how I was functioning.
About how many days in a row did that high-energy, unusually upbeat or irritable period last?

I'm honestly not really sure of the exact number of days. Um... it's a little hard to keep track of time when you're in the middle of it. It just felt like a continuous stretch where I was going a hundred miles an hour, but I couldn't tell you exactly how long it lasted.
Did that high-energy, unusually upbeat or irritable period last at least 7 days in a row?

Um, I really couldn't say for sure if it was a full seven days. Like I just mentioned, the days kind of blurred together for me. It might have been a week, or maybe just four or five days... I just didn't track it closely enough to give you a solid yes or no on that.
During that high-energy period, were you more talkative than usual?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, even though I felt like I was going a hundred miles an hour, I wasn't really... talking more than normal. I didn't notice myself being overly chatty or anything like that.
During that high-energy period, did you feel more driven than usual to start or complete projects?

Yeah, definitely. That's actually a big part of why I came in. I went from barely settling into my new apartment to... well, suddenly saying yes to mentoring sessions, taking on extra client prototypes for work, and redesigning my whole portfolio. It just felt like I had to fix my entire life in one big sprint. So, yes, I was very driven to take all of that on.
During that high-energy period, did you feel unusually confident or powerful compared with your usual self?

No, I wouldn't say that. I didn't feel... powerful or unusually confident. It was really just about having the drive to get all those projects done, not feeling like I was suddenly invincible or better at my job or anything. So, no, my confidence level was pretty much the same as usual.
During that high-energy period, did you need someone else to step in because you couldn't manage things safely or appropriately on your own?

No, um, nothing like that. I mean, I was definitely taking on way too much at once, but I was still handling it all myself. It never got to a point where I was unsafe or needed someone to step in and take over for me. I was just really busy and focused on getting it all done.
During that high-energy period, did other people clearly notice that your behavior was unusual for you?

No, I don't think so. I mean, my friends knew I was busy because I was turning down plans to work on my portfolio and the extra client stuff, but... I don't think anyone saw it as unusual behavior. They just thought I was having a really productive week at work. So, no, nobody said anything about me acting strange.
During that high-energy period, were you more active than usual in your everyday life?

Yes, definitely. Um, I was just constantly doing things. There were nights when I literally couldn't sit still. I'd be up moving furniture around, organizing and labeling all my storage bins, and then going back to my computer to tweak design mockups. And when I wasn't doing that, I was just pacing through the apartment. It just felt like stopping was impossible, like I had to keep moving.
During that high-energy period, did people close to you clearly notice that you were acting differently from your usual self?

Um, I think that's pretty much what you asked just a minute ago... but no, not really. My close friends and family didn't say anything about me acting differently. Like I mentioned earlier, they just figured I was super focused on my design work and trying to get everything done. Nobody seemed to think I was acting out of character or anything like that.
At any point in your life, have you ever had a high-energy or unusually irritable mood episode that clearly lasted at least 7 days in a row?
Um, no, I don't think so. The high-energy periods I get... they usually only last a few days, maybe four or five at the most. I don't think I've ever had one that went on for a full week straight.
During this current low period, have you lost interest or pleasure in most things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have. Um, I used to really look forward to things, like hiking at Crowders Mountain or, you know, cooking a nice meal. I even used to sketch interface ideas just for fun on my own time. But lately... I don't know, I just stare at my hiking gear or my tablet, and I just feel nothing. There's just no pull or desire to do any of it anymore.
Before this recent one, have you had other separate periods in your life when you felt this same kind of high energy and needed much less sleep?

No, I don't think so. I mean... I can't really remember any other specific times before this recent one where I felt that exact same way. Like, having that much energy and just not needing to sleep... I haven't really noticed that happening in the past.
